ImageDescription.value:
8vo. f. [1] (blank), pp. vii, [i], 130, [1], [3] (blank). Contemporary vellum. Manuscript spine title, tear on upper spine, edges spread in red and blue. Pastedown with sun-shaped and letter "M" watermark . Manuscript marks in margins of pp. 15, 52, 86. Printers' device on title page. Engraved initials, head- and tailpieces.


Work by Niccolò Maria Lisci, Curzio Inghirami’s first serious critic. Inghirami (1614-1655) had created, buried in family land, and subsequently unearthed fragments of a chronicle of Etruscan Volterra written by one Prosperus Fesulanus in 60 BC. The fragments were in ‘Etruscan,’ a language conveniently unknown to any living scholar, and told the sad story of the Roman destruction of Etruria in 60 BC. See Bib# 3584558/Fr# 353 in this collection for Inghirami’s forgery.
